entries.254916cfbc4c3054: In March 2025 the company formulated its long-term management strategy, “R.I.S.E. 2035,” and has set as its vision for 2035 the goal of continuing to provide “new experiential value created from rubber” to everyone. It names three growth drivers: strengthening brand management, creating rubber-based innovation, and building a management foundation resilient to change, and states that it will formulate a new medium-term plan for 2026 to 2030. In December 2025, in addition to the DUNLOP trademark rights for four-wheel tires in Europe, North America and Oceania, it acquired trademark usage rights in Malaysia, Singapore and Brunei, and states that from 2026 it will pursue brand management centered on the “DUNLOP” brand.

entries.a8bcc07d9a413d57: This business manufactures and sells golf equipment, such as golf clubs and golf balls, and tennis equipment, and also runs golf tournaments and golf and tennis schools. Manufacturing is handled by the company, Dunlop Golf Club Co., Ltd., Roger Cleveland Golf Company, Inc., and Dunlop Srixon Sports Manufacturing (Thailand) Co., Ltd. of Thailand, among others; sales are handled by Dunlop Sports Marketing Co., Ltd., Srixon Sports Europe Ltd., Dunlop Sports Korea Co., Ltd., and Cleveland Golf Canada Corp., among others (excluding the company, 27 companies are named in the description of the business). For the fitness business, all shares of the target company were sold in early December 2024. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥125,574 million (down 0.1% from the previous year), making it the second-largest business after tires. The company explains that golf equipment performed well, led by clubs and balls under the main SRIXON brand and the XXIO14 launched in Japan in November, offsetting a decline in revenue due to worsening market conditions in South Korea, and that revenue exceeded the previous year. Tennis equipment also saw higher revenue in Japan and Europe. Partly due to the transfer, in early December 2024, of shares in the target companies of the wellness business (excluding golf and tennis schools), revenue for the Sports Business as a whole was at roughly the same level as the previous year.

entries.dd3712771533d626: This business manufactures and sells tires and tubes for automobiles, construction vehicles, industrial vehicles, race/rally vehicles, motorcycles and other vehicles, and is the core of Sumitomo Rubber Industries, Ltd. It also includes the Automotive Business, such as puncture repair agents and air pressure warning devices. Manufacturing is handled by the company, Dunlop Retread Service Co., Ltd., and subsidiaries in Indonesia, Thailand, Brazil, South Africa, Turkey, the United States and China (Changshu and Hunan); sales are handled by the company, Dunlop Tire Co., Ltd., Sumitomo Rubber (China) Co., Ltd., Falken Tyre Europe GmbH, Sumitomo Rubber North America, Inc., and Micheldever Group Ltd. of the United Kingdom, among others (excluding the company, 63 companies are named in the description of the business). It was resolved on November 7, 2024 that Sumitomo Rubber USA, LLC of the United States would end all production activities and dissolve. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥1,043,683 million (down 0.3% from the previous year), making it the largest of the three reportable segments. The company explains that, while sales volume of domestic original equipment tires increased on firm automobile production, domestic replacement tires declined due to the withdrawal of low-priced products from the market in autumn 2024 and lower orders for off-take products. Overseas, original equipment sales fell significantly in Asia, centered on China, and replacement sales also declined in Asia and Oceania as sales were prioritized for profitability; in North America, they declined due to factors including the pass-through of tariff effects to selling prices. Meanwhile, the company states that in Europe it was able to expand sales of FALKEN-brand tires, starting with all-season tires, and that in South America sales volume grew.

entries.ecb69a9c8e90ca5f: Tires are divided into new-vehicle tires supplied to automakers and replacement tires for vehicles already on the road. No single external customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue.
entries.ee201f90bb177496: A business that makes and sells industrial and consumer products that take advantage of the properties of rubber, comprising 3 businesses: the High-Performance Rubber Business, the Consumer Goods Business and the Infrastructure Business. Manufacturing is carried out by the company, Zhongshan Zhujiao Jingmi Xiangjiao Youxian Gongsi in China, Sumirubber Vietnam, Ltd. in Vietnam, Sumirubber Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. in Malaysia and others, while sales are handled by the company, Sumigomu Sangyo Co., Ltd., Dunlop Home Products Co., Ltd., Xianggang Zhujiao Youxian Gongsi and others (8 companies listed under the description of business, excluding the company). Most products are made to forecast, and made-to-order production is limited to some products such as marine fenders. Net revenue to external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥37,804 million (a 5.0% decrease from the previous year), making it the smallest of the 3 reportable segments. The company explains that revenue fell below the previous year owing to factors such as lower sales of rubber parts for OA equipment and gloves, the withdrawal from the gas pipe business at the end of March, and the transfer in the previous year of shares in a European subsidiary that manufactures and sells medical rubber products.
